text:
You Will Need:

  • A 4x6 playing grid with words on.
  • A card showing you 9 target words and 3 poison words to avoid.
  • Two colours of counters to cover words you have guessed.
    • Call one set of counters ‘target counters’ and one set of counters ‘other counters’.
    • You could use two types of coin, buttons, pasta or anything you like.

steps.text:
• The clues must be about the meaning of the words, not the spelling or where it is in the grid.
  • You can use letters and numbers for clues if they relate to the meaning, e.g. ‘eight’ could be a clue for ‘octopus’ but not for eight-letter words.
  • You can’t say any form of a word visible on the grid, e.g. if ‘run’ is on the grid, you can’t say ‘run’, ‘running’, ‘ran’ etc until after the word ‘run’ is covered by a counter.
  • You also can’t say part of a compound word in the grid, e.g. if the word ‘blackbird’ is in the grid, you can’t say ‘bird’, ‘birdie’ or ‘songbird’.
  • You must use words that are regularly used in English sentences.

text:
How to Play

  1. Put a word grid on the table or floor between you.
  2. Player 1 looks at a target word card to see which words are target words, which words they should avoid, and which are the three poison words. They must not show the card to Player 2.
  3. Player 1 gives a single-word clue that relates to some of the target words. Player 1 also gives a number to say how many words relate to the clue. E.g. two of your words are ‘sand’ and ‘sea’ and both of these are part of a beach, so you say, ‘Beach: 2.’
  4. Player 2 thinks about the clue and talks about their thinking out loud. Player 1 is not allowed to say anything or give any face or movement hints to help. Listening to Player 2 is useful though, as it can help you understand their thinking ready for giving the next clue.
  5. When Player 2 has decided on a word (or words), they touch one word on the grid.
    • If it was a target word, put a 'target counter' on the word. Player 2 may guess another word (up to the number given by Player 1 in the clue).
    • If it was a poison word, the game ends.
    • If it was another word, put an ‘other counter’ on the word. The turn ends.
  6. On the next turn, Player 1 gives a new clue.
  7. Keep track of how many clues are given before all the target words are found.
  8. At the end of the game, add together your number of clues given and the number of ‘other words’ accidentally guessed. This is your score for the game. The lower the score, the better! If you accidentally guessed a poison word, the game ended with a high score of infinity!
  9. Play again but swapping roles so the other person has a chance to give the clues. See if you can beat your score!


Important Rule:

The player giving the clues is not allowed to help in any other way – they can’t comment on their own clues (e.g. ‘this is maybe a bit of a stretch), they can’t comment on the other player’s choices, they can’t even move their face!!

The Aim of the Game:

Player 1 gives single-word clues for the target words and Player 2 tries to guess them in as few turns as possible without accidentally choosing any of the other words. If Player 2 guesses a poison word, the game ends!
